theater: 洛陽至長安道（河內孟津）

battle.name: 討伐董卓之戰
battle.theater: 洛陽至長安道（河內孟津）
battle.brief: 初平元年關東州郡並起兵討董，盟主袁紹集十餘萬眾於陳留酸棗，諸軍按兵不進，糧秣不繼而散。董卓焚洛陽、遷都長安，孫堅北伐在陽人破敵，終在郿縣為呂布所刺。卡面埃及月牙劍未入中土，但它外彎不卡的砍劈邏輯，正與漢軍環首刀同出一源。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 討伐董卓之戰是東漢末年關東州郡聯軍與董卓控制的漢廷及其涼州軍團在初平元年（190）至初平三年（192）之間的一場戰爭，也可以說是一次未能完成的政治討伐。聯軍一方是自北而南多路響應的州郡兵：渤海太守袁紹被推為盟主，自稱車騎將軍，節制諸軍；冀州牧韓馥、陳留太守張邈、兗州刺史劉岱、豫州刺史孔伷、廣陵太守張超、泰山太守張繡、東郡太守橋瑁、山陽太守袁遺、濟北相鮑信、河內太守王匡與張楊、幽州公孫瓚部下的劉備先後起兵，各郡自行徵發鄉勇與部曲，糧秣由本州自籌，號令各自為政，盟主之位有威望而無實權，十餘萬眾的指揮鏈實際斷成數十段。董卓一方以相國身份坐鎮關中，骨幹是涼州、並州出身的舊部與羌胡精騎，麾下李傕、郭汜、張濟、樊稠、張純分道出擊，張楊、王匡等漢臣被迫曲附，遷都之後的洛陽朝廷形同虛設，中央與地方的關係完全倒置。開戰前線上還有第三種力量：荊州劉表、益州劉焉與關中的馬騰、韓遂各懷觀望，使聯軍的合圍從一開始就是環形而非球形。190年正月聯軍起兵時，雙方大體仍以漢廷正統的名義互相指斥，董卓掌朝廷、聯軍掌義兵名分，這種名義上的對立一直維持到192年董卓被刺為止。
countriesEn: The Campaign against Dong Zhuo was a war fought between the regional armies of the eastern provinces and the Han court held by Dong Zhuo together with his Liangzhou command between the first year of Chuping (190) and the third year of Chuping (192); it may equally be described as a political campaign that never really finished. The coalition side was made up of provincial and commandery troops that rose across the north and the centre. Yuan Shao, Administrator of the Sea, was pushed forward as leader of the coalition, styled himself General of Chariots and Cavalry, and nominally directed the assembled armies; the Governor of Ji, Han Fu, the Administrator of Chenliu, Zhang Miao, the Inspector of Yanzhou, Liu Dai, the Inspector of Yuzhou, Kong Ji, the Administrator of Guangling, Zhang Chao, the Administrator of Taishan, Zhang Xiu, the Administrator of Dongjun, Qiao Mao, the Administrator of Shanyang, Yuan Yi, the Minor Protector of Jibei, Bao Xin, the Administrator of Henei, Wang Kuang and Zhang Yang, and the men under Gongsun Zan in Youzhou together with Liu Bei who rose in Pingyuan all answered the call in turn. Each commandery recruited its own villagers and its own armed followers, each province found its own grain, and each commander issued his own orders. The title of leader carried prestige but no real power, and the chain of command over an army said to number more than a hundred thousand men was in fact broken into several dozen separate segments. Dong Zhuo's side sat at the centre of the empire in the office of Chancellor, its backbone being veterans from Liangzhou and Bingzhou together with the elite Qiang and Hu cavalry; his commanders Li Jue, Guo Si, Zhang Ji, Fan Chou and Zhang Chun operated on separate lines, Han officials such as Zhang Yang and Wang Kuang were obliged to bend to him, and after the move west the court at Luoyang was a shell, the relation between centre and provinces completely inverted. A third force stood on the line before the fighting began: Liu Biao in Jingzhou, Liu Yan in Yi Province, and Ma Teng and Han Sui in the western regions all watched and waited, so that the encirclement of Dong Zhuo was a ring and never a sphere. When the coalition rose in the first month of Chuping, both sides still denounced each other in the name of the legitimate Han court, Dong Zhuo holding the court and the coalition holding the banner of righteous troops, and that nominal opposition lasted until Dong Zhuo was run through in 192.
people: 董卓是全場的起點，也是全場的終點。他出身涼州邊地，189年大將軍何進與袁紹謀誅宦官時奉召率兵入洛陽，藉勤王之名取得禁軍控制權，旋廢少帝、立獻帝，誅何氏一族，獨掌軍政大柄；關東起兵之後，他先以兵威脅迫關中與豫北的糧道，再焚宗廟陵寢及宮室，遷都長安，把洛陽留成廢墟；聯軍逼近時他採取守而不戰、拖住聯軍的辦法，最後卻死於自己建立的信任關係上。呂布本是並州騎將，先殺丁原歸董，192年受司徒王允策劃，在郿縣宮中刺殺董卓，事後又與王允互相猜忌而走向對立。王允是策劃者，出身太原王氏，董卓死後數月掌控朝廷，處置失當，終於在李傕郭汜反攻長安時兵敗被殺，策劃者死在自己製造的亂局裡。聯軍一端，袁紹以渤海兵起家，先受韓馥讓出的冀州，又借聯軍之號收攏河北，成為日後統一北方者；其弟袁術以勇力爭盟主之位，兄弟交惡直接瓦解了聯軍的基本盤。曹操在初平元年率兵五千赴酸棗，是唯一當場指出聯軍十餘萬眾按兵不進、器械糧秣不備的人，他勸聯軍進兵並提出斷敵糧道的方案未被採納，此後以兗州為根據地，收編青州降眾、迎獻帝遷許都，最後承接了董卓之死留下的空缺。孫堅是聯軍中真正打到前線的將領，191年在陽人擊破董卓前軍，斬都督華雄，進洛陽修復宗廟陵寢，卻在192年攻荊州時中流矢死於峴山，部曲由其子孫策、孫權接手入江東。另有公孫瓚在幽州起兵、追擊董卓至潁陽一線而止，與袁紹爭奪冀州；劉表在荊州觀望並屢違盟約；荀彧、荀攸在曹操帳中籌劃迎帝還都；賈詡在董卓死後勸李傕郭汜迎獻帝以為籌碼；馬騰、韓遂在關西響應起兵又與董卓暗中往來。這些人各自的取捨，最後都成了這場戰爭的走向。
peopleEn: Dong Zhuo was the beginning of the whole affair and also its end. A native of the frontier in Liangzhou, he was summoned in 189 with his troops to Luoyang when the General-in-Chief He Jin and Yuan Shao plotted to destroy the eunuchs; taking the name of a rescuer of the dynasty he gained control of the imperial guards, deposed the young emperor, enthroned Xian, killed the He clan and took the army and the government into his own hands. After the eastern provinces rose he first used his troops to threaten the grain roads of Guanzhong and northern Henan, then burned the ancestral temple, the imperial tombs and the palaces, moved the capital west to Chang'an and left Luoyang a ruin. When the coalition closed in he chose to hold and to wait rather than to fight, and in the end he died through the trust relationships he himself had built. Lü Bu was a cavalry officer from Bingzhou who killed Ding Yuan in order to join Dong Zhuo; in 192 he was drawn into the plot of the Minister of Works Wang Yun and ran Dong Zhuo through in the palace at Meixian, and he afterwards fell to mutual suspicion with Wang Yun himself. Wang Yun was the plotter, of the Wang clan of Taiyuan; for the few months after Dong Zhuo's death he held the court, handled the business badly, and was killed when Li Jue and Guo Si counter-attacked Chang'an, so that the plotter died in the disorder he had made. On the coalition side, Yuan Shao rose from the troops of the Sea, took over Ji from Han Fu, and used the banner of the coalition to gather Hebei, becoming the man who would later unite the north. His younger brother Yuan Shu, a braver soldier, fought for the position of leader of the coalition, and the quarrel between the two brothers broke the foundation of the coalition outright. Cao Cao marched to Suanzao with five thousand men in the first year of Chuping and was the only man present who stated plainly that more than a hundred thousand troops stood there without moving and that weapons and grain were not in readiness; his advice to advance and his plan to cut the enemy's supply road were not taken up, and he went on to make Yanzhou his base, absorb the surrendered men of Qingzhou, and bring the emperor to Xu, finally taking over the vacancy left by Dong Zhuo's death. Sun Jian was the commander of the coalition who really reached the front. In 191 he broke Dong Zhuo's vanguard at Yangren and cut down the Director Hua Xiong, entered Luoyang and repaired the ancestral temple and the tombs, and in 192 was killed by an arrow at Xianshan while attacking Jingzhou, his troops passing to his sons Sun Ce and Sun Quan, who carried them into Jiangdong. Others: Gongsun Zan rose in Youzhou and pursued Dong Zhuo as far as the Yingyang line before stopping, then fought Yuan Shao for Ji; Liu Biao watched from Jingzhou and broke his agreements more than once; Xun Yu and Xun You planned in Cao Cao's camp to bring the emperor home; Jia Xu advised Li Jue and Guo Si after Dong Zhuo's death to receive the emperor as a bargaining counter; Ma Teng and Han Sui answered the call in the west and yet kept up secret dealings with Dong Zhuo. The choices each of these made were in the end the direction of this war.
kits: 卡面這件埃及月牙劍是古埃及的短兵，學界一般稱為 khopesh，希臘史料中相近形制的劍則稱 kopis。它是外彎的單刃，刃線向內凹成月牙，柄端常作梨形或錘形，部分形制在柄前加寬作護手；長度多在五十至六十公分上下，以銅合金與青銅製品為主，少數用鐵。它在古埃及第二王朝的兵器譜系中已有雛形，新王國時期的壁畫與墓葬繪畫大量描繪了持劍者的樣貌。它是砍劈用的兵器：因為刃口外彎，砍入骨盾之後不必像直刃那樣費力扭拔，這正是它比直劍更早成熟的原因；必要時也可作刺擊之用。由於形制相近，埃及月牙劍與希臘早期彎劍、其後高盧彎刀一路的兵器常被連成一條譜系，中間的傳播細節仍多靠推測。公元190年的洛陽前線上沒有這件兵器：漢軍步卒配的是環首刀、雙刃直劍與青銅劍，長兵器是矛、戟、戈，射手用弓、弩與強弩，護具是札甲、皮革甲以及大盾、梟盾，騎兵則來自並州與涼州。攻城方面有雲梯、撞車與飛樓，渡河與運糧依靠舟船與車馬，軍令與營汛靠旗鼓、金柝與號角。董卓部將在關東各線的實際戰鬥，多是騎兵突襲以及焚燒破壞之後的追擊；孫堅在陽人使用的火攻，與董卓焚洛陽的刻意破壞，同屬火在戰爭中的用法。環首刀與月牙劍分處歐亞兩端，卻共享同一條工程判準：砍下去要拔得回來。
kitsEn: The Egyptian khopesh on the card was a short weapon of ancient Egypt, generally called a khopesh in scholarship, while Greek sources use the name kopis for a closely similar form. It was a single-edged blade curved outward, the edge line drawn inward into a crescent, the pommel often pear-shaped or knobbed, and in some examples widened in front of the grip to serve as a guard; the length is generally fifty to sixty centimetres, with copper alloy and bronze the common materials and iron used for a minority. It already had ancestors in the weapon inventory of the Second Dynasty, and wall paintings and tomb scenes of the New Kingdom show the sword-bearer in quantity. It was a chopping weapon: because the edge curves outward, a blow that lands in bone or shield does not have to be twisted free as it would with a straight edge, and that is exactly why it matured before the straight sword; it could also be used for the thrust when required. Because the forms are close, the Egyptian khopesh, the early Greek curved sword and the later Gallic falcata are often strung into a single lineage, though the details of how it travelled remain largely conjectural. The weapon on the card was not present on the Luoyang front in AD 190. Han infantry carried ring-pommel sabres, double-edged straight jians and bronze swords, with spears, ji and ge as the long weapons, bows, crossbows and strong crossbows in the hands of the shooters, and mail and leather armour together with large shields and light wicker shields for protection, the cavalry coming from Bingzhou and Liangzhou. The siege train included scaling ladders, battering rams and tall towers, river crossings and the movement of grain depended on boats and draft animals, and orders and camp routine were kept by drums, gongs and signal horns. The actual fighting of Dong Zhuo's commanders on the eastern lines consisted largely of cavalry shock and of pursuit after burning and destruction; the fire attack used by Sun Jian at Yangren belongs to the same use of fire in war as the deliberate destruction of Luoyang by Dong Zhuo. The ring-pommel sabre and the khopesh sit at the two ends of Eurasia, and share a single engineering judgement: a blow that lands must be able to be withdrawn again.
tactics: 聯軍的戰術可以分三層。第一層是集結與僵持：初平元年正月各州郡同時起兵，卻沒有約定的集結地與指揮程序，直至袁紹被推為盟主，諸軍才在陳留酸棗會合，連營數十重，人數以十餘萬計；但各軍自備糧秣、兵器未備，帳中每日宴飲而無一軍肯先出，曹操以義兵持疑而不進、失天下之望相責，聯軍仍不見采行，於是在原地空耗數月，最後因劉岱與橋瑁爭兵互相殺害、張邈責其違約而散夥。第二層是幾條零散的外線：孫堅自廬江北上，在梁東受挫之後抓住董卓分兵之機，於191年在陽人擊破前軍、斬都督華雄，隨後直抵洛陽修治宗廟陵寢，並拒絕董卓的求和；袁紹在河內與董卓隔黃河相持，又與劉表約定夾擊，劉表按兵不動，聯軍失去兩面合擊的機會；公孫瓚在幽州追擊董卓至潁陽一線而止，關西的馬騰、韓遂起兵之後又各自與董卓往來。第三層是董卓的守勢與宮廷的突擊：董卓放棄洛陽，焚燒宮室、遷都長安，據潼關與秦嶺的形勝、絕糧道、築深溝高壘，把洛陽與豫州之間的攻城拖成一場聯軍的糧秣競賽；到192年他倚重羌胡精騎與宮中宿衛，卻被王允利用其對部將的疑心，誘其入朝，由呂布一擊而定其命。整體看，聯軍輸在沒有把十餘萬人變成一支軍隊：號令不統一、糧秣不統一、戰爭目標也不統一，於是每一次集兵都是一次重新分配利益的機會。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the coalition fall into three layers. The first was assembly and deadlock. In the first month of Chuping the provinces rose at the same time but had agreed neither on a place of assembly nor on any procedure of command; only after Yuan Shao was pushed forward as leader did the armies come together at Suanzao in Chenliu, camp after camp over tens of li, with the numbers put at more than a hundred thousand. Yet each army brought its own grain, the weapons were not in readiness, and in the tents there was daily feasting while not one contingent would march out first. Cao Cao blamed them for holding back as righteous troops and for forfeiting the regard of the realm, and it was still not adopted. The months were therefore wasted on the spot, and the coalition came apart at last after Liu Dai and Qiao Mao killed one another over troops and Zhang Miao accused him of breaking the agreement. The second layer consisted of several scattered outer lines. Sun Jian marched north from Lujiang, recovered from the reverse at Liangdong, seized the moment when Dong Zhuo had split his forces, broke the vanguard at Yangren in 191 and cut down the Director Hua Xiong, then went straight to Luoyang to repair the ancestral temple and the tombs and refused Dong Zhuo's offer of peace. Yuan Shao faced Dong Zhuo across the Yellow River at Henei, and arranged with Liu Biao to strike from both sides, but Liu Biao did not move and the coalition lost the chance of the double attack. Gongsun Zan pursued Dong Zhuo in Youzhou as far as the Yingyang line and stopped, while Ma Teng and Han Sui, having risen in the west, went back to private dealings with Dong Zhuo. The third layer was Dong Zhuo's defensive posture and the stroke in the palace. He gave up Luoyang, burned the palaces, moved the capital to Chang'an, took advantage of the terrain of Tong Pass and the Qinling range, cut the supply road and built deep ditches and high ramparts, turning the siege of Luoyang into a race in grain for the coalition. By 192 he relied on the elite Qiang and Hu cavalry and the palace guard, yet Wang Yun used his suspicion of his own officers to lure him to court, and one stroke of Lü Bu settled the matter. Taken as a whole, the coalition lost because it never turned more than a hundred thousand men into an army: the orders were not one, the grain was not one, the object of the war was not one, and so every muster was another chance to divide the spoils anew.
data: 時間線是這場戰爭最清楚的刻度：中平元年（189）四月靈帝去世，少帝即位，何氏臨朝；八月大將軍何進與袁紹謀誅宦官，召董卓入京為外援；九月宦官搶先弒殺何進，董卓兵入洛陽，廢少帝為弘農王、立陳留王劉協為帝；初平元年（190）正月關東州郡起兵，曹操率兵五千至酸棗，見諸侯兵十餘萬而無一人敢先登；同年二月董卓焚宗廟陵寢及宮室，遷都長安；初平二年（191）孫堅在陽人破董卓軍、斬都督華雄，進洛陽修宗廟，袁紹與劉表相約夾擊不成；初平三年（192）四月董卓入朝被呂布刺殺於郿縣，六月李傕郭汜反攻長安、王允死，其後二年遷帝於弘農、安邑，直到建安元年（196）曹操迎獻帝遷都許都。數字上，聯軍在酸棗會師者史稱十餘萬，但各州兵不相屬，能同時調動者遠少於此；曹操自領之兵為五千，這個比例說明聯軍的兵力集中在名義而不在編制。孫堅部是袁術麾下的偏師，數千至萬餘人，卻在正面戰鬥中給了董卓唯一一次實質挫敗。董卓軍以涼州精騎與羌胡部眾為骨幹，人數常被記為數萬。地理上，酸棗至洛陽約二百餘里，洛陽至長安逾一千餘里，中隔潼關與崤函之險；黃河渡口在平陰與孟津，聯軍北上與東進的糧道都要過河，這是董卓寧可放棄洛陽也不願被夾擊的地理理由。真正的損失並不在戰場：聯軍自起兵到解散，絕大多數時間消耗在集結、爭執與等待上，兩年之間的正面交鋒只集中在陽人、洛陽與郿縣數處。
dataEn: The chronology is the clearest measuring line for this war. In the fourth month of Zhongping (189) the Emperor Ling died, the child emperor took the throne and the Empress Dowager He held the court; in the eighth month the General-in-Chief He Jin and Yuan Shao plotted to destroy the eunuchs and summoned Dong Zhuo to the capital as external support; in the ninth month the eunuchs struck first and killed He Jin, Dong Zhuo's troops entered Luoyang, the child emperor was demoted to King of Hongnong and the King of Chenliu, Liu Xie, was set on the throne. In the first month of Chuping (190) the eastern provinces rose, Cao Cao reached Suanzao with five thousand men and saw the armies of the lords, more than a hundred thousand of them, with not one willing to lead the charge; in the second month of the same year Dong Zhuo burned the ancestral temple, the tombs and the palaces and moved the capital to Chang'an. In the second year of Chuping (191) Sun Jian broke Dong Zhuo's army at Yangren and cut down the Director Hua Xiong, entered Luoyang and repaired the ancestral temple, and the arrangement between Yuan Shao and Liu Biao to strike together came to nothing. In the fourth month of the third year of Chuping (192) Dong Zhuo was run through at Meixian by Lü Bu; in the sixth month Li Jue and Guo Si counter-attacked Chang'an and Wang Yun died, and the court was moved to Hongnong and then Anyi over the following two years, until in the first year of Jian'an (196) Cao Cao brought the emperor to Xu. On numbers: the muster at Suanzao is recorded in the histories as more than a hundred thousand men, but the provincial armies were not subordinate to one another and far fewer could be moved at once; Cao Cao brought five thousand of his own, and that ratio shows the coalition's strength lay in its name rather than in its organisation. Sun Jian's force was a detachment in Yuan Shu's service, numbering several thousand to a little over ten thousand, and yet it gave Dong Zhuo his one substantive reverse in open battle. Dong Zhuo's army had as its backbone the picked Liangzhou cavalry and the Qiang and Hu levies, and is often put at several tens of thousands. As for geography, Suanzao lies about two hundred li from Luoyang and Luoyang more than a thousand li from Chang'an, with Tong Pass and the Hanguo heights between them; the crossings of the Yellow River were at Pingyin and Mengjin, and every grain road by which the coalition marched north or east had to cross the river, which was the geographical reason Dong Zhuo would rather abandon Luoyang than be taken between two armies. The real losses were not on the battlefield. From the rising to the dispersal the coalition spent the great part of its time on assembly, quarrelling and waiting, and between the two years the actual clashes were confined to Yangren, Luoyang and Meixian.
cause: 起兵的原因可以分三層。最外層是宮廷的變故：189年靈帝死，何進以大將軍掌兵，卻無力制宦官，遂與袁紹謀召外兵入京；宦官搶先弒殺何進，董卓因此以勤王之名率兵入洛陽，旋廢立天子、誅戮朝臣，專擅朝政，關東州郡乃以清除君側、討誅逆臣的名義起兵。第二層是董卓的統治方式：他以涼州與羌胡武力壓服關東士族，抽調京畿與州郡的兵備財貨，刑罰任性，朝士受辱，遷都長安更使洛陽盡成焦土，關東士人與涼州將校之間的舊怨、朝臣與權臣之間的權力衝突，於是匯成同一條戰線；董卓入洛之初誅殺宦官張讓等以收人心，恰恰說明他清楚自己必須靠士人之心立足，卻又始終不肯讓士人分享權力。第三層是聯軍自身無法解決的問題：關東各州起兵是各懷心思的集合體，袁紹與袁術兄弟有爭權之隙，劉表只想保住荊州，韓馥捨不得冀州，劉岱與橋瑁各不相讓，這些矛盾在共誅董卓的口號下暫時被壓住，卻在糧秣分配與誰先進攻的問題上立刻爆發。董卓正是看準了這點，才敢放棄洛陽、把戰線拉成長線，靜待聯軍自行瓦解。戰爭的真正起因因此不是某一場戰鬥，而是一次在錯的時間、用錯的組織方式發起的政治行動。
causeEn: The reasons for the rising can be set out in three layers. The outermost was a change in the palace. In 189 the Emperor Ling died; He Jin took the army as General-in-Chief but had no power over the eunuchs, and so he and Yuan Shao plotted to summon troops from outside. The eunuchs struck first and killed He Jin, which gave Dong Zhuo the pretext of a rescuer to march into Luoyang; he then deposed and enthroned emperors, killed ministers, monopolised the government, and the eastern provinces rose in the name of clearing the sovereign's side of evil ministers and punishing rebels. The second layer was the manner of Dong Zhuo's rule. He used Liangzhou and Qiang and Hu force to overbear the scholar-gentry of the east, drew the arms and wealth of the capital region and the provinces to himself, inflicted punishment arbitrarily, humiliated the court, and the move of the capital to Chang'an turned Luoyang into scorched ground; the old enmity between the scholar-gentry of the east and the officers of Liangzhou, and the struggle for power between the ministers and the usurper, were thus gathered into a single front. That Dong Zhuo killed the eunuch Zhang Rang and the rest on entering Luoyang shows plainly that he knew he had to stand on the good will of the scholars, and that he yet never intended to share power with them. The third layer was a problem the coalition could not solve for itself. The rising of the provinces was a gathering of men each with his own purpose: a quarrel for precedence between the brothers Yuan Shao and Yuan Shu, Liu Biao intent only on holding Jingzhou, Han Fu unwilling to surrender Ji, Liu Dai and Qiao Mao unable to yield to each other. These conflicts were held down for a while beneath the slogan of joint execution against Dong Zhuo, and broke out at once over the distribution of grain and over who should advance first. It was precisely here that Dong Zhuo saw his advantage, and dared to abandon Luoyang, stretch the line out and wait for the coalition to dissolve of its own accord. The true cause of the war was therefore not any single engagement, but a political action launched at the wrong moment and with the wrong organisation.
impact: 這場戰爭最直接的結果是打碎了帝國的秩序，而受益者並不是聯軍。董卓死後，聯軍失去共同敵人，數月之內名存實亡：袁紹與袁術兄弟反目，公孫瓚與袁紹爭冀州，劉表、劉焉、馬騰、韓遂各自割據，孫策承父兵入江東，曹操收青州降眾據兗州，州牧、刺史手中同時握著兵權與財賦，中央朝廷再無力調動任何一州一郡。制度上，這是州郡勢力合法化並且永久化的起點；東漢的徵兵、罷兵與轉運制度在混戰中失效，軍隊私屬化，部曲與屯田成為爭奪的對象，曹操在建安年間推行屯田，正是對聯軍因糧秣而崩潰的直接教訓。洛陽作為帝都的樞紐功能中斷了數十年，宮室、宗廟與陵寢長期失修，士人南渡、經典散佚，形成建安文風的蒼涼底色；中原士族與江南士族集團各自成形，隋唐以後南北對峙的文化地理，源頭正在這幾年。外來武力同樣留下痕跡：董卓的涼州軍與羌胡部眾在關中盤據，關東士人受其凌逼，兩種人群的敵意延續到曹魏時代的西涼與關中戰爭裡，又成為曹丕代漢時不得不解決的軍隊歸屬問題。最後說到卡面這件月牙劍：它在這場戰爭裡完全沒有角色，也不可能有角色，因為它在公元190年的東亞早已是兩千年前的古物；但它提醒我們，刃的形制——外彎、砍擊、不卡骨——在歐亞兩端被各自獨立解決，而決定這場戰爭勝負的卻是糧秣、號令與一個暴政者的死。
impactEn: The most direct effect of this war was the smashing of the order of the empire, and the beneficiaries were not the coalition. Once Dong Zhuo was dead the coalition lost its common enemy and within a few months existed in name only: the brothers Yuan Shao and Yuan Shu quarrelled, Gongsun Zan and Yuan Shao fought for Ji, Liu Biao, Liu Yan, Ma Teng and Han Sui each held their own territory, Sun Ce carried his father's troops into Jiangdong, Cao Cao absorbed the surrendered men of Qingzhou and based himself in Yanzhou, and the provincial governors and inspectors now held the soldiers and the revenue at once, while the central court could no longer move a single commandery or province. In institutional terms this was the point at which the power of the provinces became legitimate and permanent. The Han institutions of recruitment, discharge and transport broke down amid the fighting, armies became private property, and commanderies and dependent followers were objects of contention; Cao Cao's promotion of tuntian during the Jian'an years was a direct lesson drawn from the way the coalition had collapsed for want of grain. Luoyang's role as the hinge of the imperial capital was interrupted for decades; the palaces, the ancestral temple and the tombs fell into long disrepair, scholars moved south and the classics dispersed, and the plain severity of the Jian'an literary style was made out of that; the scholar groups of the central plain and of the south formed separately, and the cultural geography of the north-south division of later Sui and Tang has its source in these few years. Foreign military power left its trace as well. The Liangzhou troops and the Qiang and Hu levies of Dong Zhuo entrenched themselves in Guanzhong, the scholars of the east were ground down by them, and the hostility between the two groups of people ran on into the wars of Xiliang and Guanzhong in the Cao Wei period, and became the problem of where the armies were to belong when Cao Pi replaced the Han. Last of all, the khopesh on the card had no part in this war and could not have had one, for in AD 190 in East Asia it was already an artefact two thousand years old. It does make the point that the shape of a blade, curved outward, for chopping, not catching in bone, was solved independently at the two ends of Eurasia, whereas what decided this war was grain, orders and the death of a usurper.
result: 打到最後：初平三年（192）四月，董卓入朝，呂布持矛自側刺之，伏兵四起，董卓死於郿縣，屍體被張讓等在城東焚化，沒有得到任何葬禮；聯軍的原始目標就此消失。接著是比原戰爭更混亂的第二回合：李傕郭汜利用聯軍留在關中的涼州兵的宿怨反攻長安，殺王允，賈詡勸二人迎獻帝於弘農，於是關中、關東、荊州、江南各自割據的分裂局面被坐實，直到建安元年曹操迎帝遷許，才重新有一個名義上的中心。孫堅在修好宗廟陵寢之後的次年戰死於峴山，其部曲由孫策、孫權接手；袁紹在河北收拾了公孫瓚，又於官渡勝曹操；袁術稱帝僅兩年而敗亡；曹操則在兗州、豫州先後建立起可持續的兵源與糧食。回頭看，這場戰爭在戰術層面幾乎沒有決定性的會戰，卻在兩個方面改寫了歷史：一是除掉了一個把漢廷當作戰利品的權臣，使後來的權臣吸取教訓，改以挾天子以令諸侯的方式取得合法性；二是暴露了以義兵號召、以私兵成軍的聯軍模式在後勤與指揮上的致命缺陷，此後漢末群雄的競爭因此全都壓在屯田、糧道與內部整頓上。洛陽殘破、長安空虛、新都未立，漢室的招牌還掛著，實際的天下卻已經被瓜分完畢。卡面月牙劍所代表的那種古老的、講究砍下去拔得回來的單刃，在這場戰爭裡只是考古學上的旁證；真正決定結局的，是糧秣、陰謀與一柄刺穿喉嚨的矛。
resultEn: In the end: in the fourth month of the third year of Chuping (192) Dong Zhuo came to court, Lü Bu thrust a spear at him from the side, the ambush closed in from every quarter, and Dong Zhuo died at Meixian; his body was taken by Zhang Rang and the others and burned in the eastern quarter of the city, and he received no funeral. The original object of the coalition had simply vanished. What followed was a second round more confused than the first: Li Jue and Guo Si used the old grievances of the Liangzhou soldiers the coalition had left in Guanzhong to counter-attack Chang'an and killed Wang Yun; Jia Xu advised them to receive the emperor at Hongnong, and the division between Guanzhong, the east, Jingzhou and Jiangnan was thus made permanent, until in the first year of Jian'an Cao Cao brought the emperor to Xu and there was once again a centre in name. Sun Jian was killed at Xianshan in the year after he had repaired the ancestral temple and the tombs, his troops passing to Sun Ce and Sun Quan; Yuan Shao settled Gongsun Zan in Hebei and then defeated Cao Cao at Guandu; Yuan Shu proclaimed himself emperor and was destroyed within two years; Cao Cao built up a durable supply of men and grain in Yanzhou and Yu Province. Looked at again, this war produced almost no decisive engagement at the tactical level, yet it rewrote history in two ways. It removed a usurper who treated the Han court as spoils of war, so that the usurpers who came after learned the lesson and sought legitimacy by holding the emperor in their hands and issuing orders in his name. And it exposed the fatal weakness, in supply and in command, of a coalition called out by the banner of righteousness but raised from private soldiers; from then on the competition among the warlords of late Han was pressed entirely onto tuntian, the grain roads and internal reform. Luoyang lay in ruins, Chang'an stood empty, no new capital had been built, the signboard of the Han still hung, and the realm had already been divided up. The old single-edged blade on the card, careful to be withdrawn again after a blow, was nothing but an archaeological bystander in this war. What really settled the outcome was grain, conspiracy and one spear driven through a throat.
